evals.expected_output: The agent dispatches a single generic subagent with the embedded investigation briefing (question filled in, read-only constraint, five-section output format) and relays the subagent's report back verbatim, without doing its own separate exploration in the main conversation.
expectations: The agent dispatches a subagent (e.g. via the Agent tool) rather than searching the repo itself in the main conversation
The dispatch prompt includes the investigation strategy (anchors, cheap search first, progressive narrowing, evidence-based tracing) and a read-only/no-edit constraint
The dispatch prompt does not hardcode a specific tech stack (e.g. does not assume Java/Spring unless the question itself named it)
The final report returned to the user has exactly the five sections: Likely owner, Functionality path, Evidence, Unknowns, Next best action
The agent does not perform its own additional file edits or writes

evals.expected_output: Since no question was given, the agent asks the user what they want located instead of dispatching a subagent on an empty query.
expectations: The agent asks a clarifying question for the missing investigation target
The agent does not dispatch a subagent before a question is provided
